Statement of Work — Sample Client Engagement – CRM Rollout

DRAFT generated 7/24/2026 — review all terms before sending. Timeline Jul 23, 2026 → Sep 3, 2026 (committed date incl. contingency: Sep 9, 2026).

1. Overview & Objectives

This Statement of Work covers a CRM Rollout engagement to be delivered between July 23, 2026 and September 3, 2026. The engagement is designed to move the client from initial discovery through solution design, data migration, testing, and go-live, culminating in a fully operational CRM system supported by a defined hypercare period. The objective is to ensure a structured, well-documented transition to the new CRM with clear requirements traceability and stakeholder alignment at each stage.

2. Scope of Work & Deliverables

The scope of work is organized into a sequence of stages, beginning with kick-off and discovery and progressing through stakeholder interviews, requirements gathering, solution design, data mapping, integration testing, and go-live with hypercare support. Each stage produces a defined deliverable, such as discovery notes, signed requirements, or a solution design document, to ensure traceability and a shared understanding of progress. The engagement formally concludes with project closure once all deliverables have been accepted and the live system is operating as intended.

Fixed price: $90,967 (risk-adjusted at P80 effort basis). 10. Acceptance Process & Defect Severity

Each deliverable identified in the scope table will be submitted to the client for review, with acceptance confirmed in writing within a mutually agreed review period. A deliverable will be deemed accepted if the client does not provide written feedback or objections within that period. Final project closure will require formal client sign-off confirming that all deliverables have been received and the live system is functioning as specified.

SeverityDefinitionAcceptance gate
S1 — CriticalBlocks a primary flow or corrupts data; no workaround.Zero open S1 at acceptance.
S2 — MajorA committed criterion fails; workaround exists but is unreasonable for daily use.Accepted only with a written remediation date.
S3 — MinorCosmetic-plus: wrong text, layout, non-blocking validation gaps.Logged; scheduled into support/hypercare.
S4 — CosmeticTrivial visual polish with no functional impact.Does not affect acceptance.

11. Change Control

Any changes to the scope, timeline, or deliverables described in this Statement of Work must be submitted in writing and evaluated for impact on cost, schedule, and resources. No change will be implemented until both parties have agreed to and signed a corresponding change order. This process ensures that adjustments are documented and that the fixed-price commercial terms remain aligned with the agreed scope.

Appendix — Key Delivery Risks

  • Client sandbox access may slip past kickoff

Appendix — User Stories & Acceptance Criteria

Each story is accepted when its acceptance criteria pass in the designated environment. Criteria marked error/edge define graceful failure behaviour and boundary handling and are part of the committed scope.

Personas: Client Operations Manager — Runs the day-to-day case operation; accepts migrated data and configured workflows.; Client Data Steward — Owns legacy data quality; approves field mappings and cleanup decisions.; Client Operations SME — Front-line process expert; validates that configured flows match real work.; Client UAT Coordinator — Schedules client testers and owns UAT evidence and sign-off.; Engagement Manager — Delivery-side governance role — responsible for charter, cadence and cutover (process stories).; Business Analyst — Delivery-side elicitation role — responsible for interviews and the requirements register (process stories).; Solution Architect — Delivery-side design authority — responsible for the approved solution design (process stories).; QA & Test Lead — Delivery-side test role — responsible for integration test execution and results (process stories).

EP-2 — Solution Design & Data Readiness

IDStory & acceptance criteriaWBS trace
US-5As a Client Data Steward, I want to review and approve the field-level mapping from the legacy system before migration is built, so that migrated records mean the same thing in the new CRM as they did in the old one.
  • happy — Given the legacy schema extract And the target object model, When the mapping spec is complete, Then every in-scope field has a target, a transform rule or an explicit drop decision And I approve the spec within 5 business days
  • error — Given a field whose sampled values violate its stated rule in more than 2% of rows, When profiling runs, Then the field is flagged with concrete examples And a cleanup or transform decision is recorded before the spec is approved
  • edge — Edge — orphaned records: Given legacy records whose parent account no longer exists, When mapping is defined, Then the spec states whether they attach to a holding account or are excluded And the chosen rule appears in the reconciliation report
NFRs: Mapping spec lists per-field data ownership; personally identifiable fields are marked for masked display outside production
 2.2 Data Mapping

EP-3 — Build, Verify & Adopt

IDStory & acceptance criteriaWBS trace
US-6As a Client Operations Manager, I want to work migrated case records with full history in the new CRM, so that my team continues daily operations without reconstructing history by hand.
  • happy — Given the approved design And the approved mapping spec, When migration into the UAT environment completes, Then record counts reconcile to the legacy source within 0.1% per object And every migrated case shows owner, status and full activity history And a reconciliation report with per-object counts is produced within 24 hours of the run
  • error — Given a legacy record that fails validation (missing owner or malformed date), When the migration runs, Then the record is quarantined to an exceptions file stating source row, rule violated and suggested fix And the run completes without aborting
  • edge — Edge — boundary date: Given records created exactly 24 months before the cutover date, When the extract is built, Then boundary records are included and older records excluded And both totals appear in the reconciliation report
  • perf — Given 50 concurrent users in the UAT environment, When a case page is opened, Then p95 page render completes in 2 seconds or less measured over a 30-minute test window
NFRs: p95 case page render ≤ 2 s at 50 concurrent users; Audit trail on case status changes retained 24 months
 3.1.1 Data migration build & dry run
US-10As a Client Operations SME, I want to raise cases that route themselves to the right queue with the fields my process needs, so that agents work from one queue without re-triaging misrouted cases.
  • happy — Given a new case with a category And all required fields completed, When the case is saved, Then it is assigned to the queue mapped for that category within 5 seconds And the assignment appears in the case history with the rule name
  • error — Given a case missing a required field, When a save is attempted, Then the save is rejected with the missing field named inline And no partial case record is created
  • edge — Edge — unmapped category: Given a case whose category has no queue mapping, When the case is saved, Then it routes to the triage queue And a daily report lists unmapped-category cases with their counts
NFRs: Queue assignment decision recorded in case history for every routed case
 3.1.2 Core workflow configuration
US-11As a Client Operations Manager, I want to see queue visibility that matches each person's role, so that agents see their own work while I keep oversight across all queues.
  • happy — Given an agent assigned to the billing queue, When they open the case list, Then only billing-queue cases are listed And the queue total matches the manager view for that queue
  • error — Given an agent opens a direct link to a case outside their queue, When access is evaluated, Then the case is not displayed And the attempt is recorded in the access log with user and timestamp
  • edge — Edge — role change mid-shift: Given an agent is moved to another queue, When their next list refresh occurs, Then the new queue's cases appear and the old queue's disappear within 15 minutes without a re-login
NFRs: Access log retained 12 months and exportable by the manager role
 3.1.3 Access model & queue setup
US-12As a Client UAT Coordinator, I want to have every tester trained in the loaded UAT environment before they execute cases, so that UAT results measure the system, not the testers' unfamiliarity.
  • happy — Given the UAT environment is loaded with migrated sample data, When the training session completes, Then every tester has executed one guided case end-to-end And attendance plus a score of at least 7 of 10 on the check are recorded per tester
  • error — Given a tester scores below 7 of 10 on the check, When results are recorded, Then a repeat session is booked within 2 business days And that tester executes UAT cases only after passing
  • edge — Edge — late joiner: Given a tester joins after the session, When they are onboarded, Then they complete the recorded session and the check before executing any case And the UAT plan notes the late start
NFRs: Training attendance and scores recorded per tester and visible to the engagement manager
 3.3.1 Tester training session
US-8As a Client UAT Coordinator, I want to run the scripted UAT cases with evidence captured against each acceptance criterion, so that acceptance is evidenced by our own staff executing real scenarios.
  • happy — Given the UAT entry criteria are met And the testers passed training, When the UAT window closes, Then every scripted case has a recorded pass/fail result with evidence attached And sign-off is granted only with zero open S1/S2 defects
  • error — Given a case fails during execution, When the defect is logged, Then the record names the failing step, expected versus actual and a severity And a retest is scheduled within 2 business days of the fix
  • edge — Edge — tester shortfall: Given fewer than the planned testers are available in a UAT week, When the shortfall is known, Then the window is re-planned with the engagement manager within 1 business day And the sign-off date moves visibly in the plan rather than compressing coverage
NFRs: Evidence (screenshot or export) attached to every executed case result
 3.3.2 UAT execution — migrated data & workflows
US-13As a Client UAT Coordinator, I want to run a daily triage of failed cases with severities, owners and a published burn-down, so that defects move to closure on a visible clock instead of piling up.
  • happy — Given failed UAT cases from the day's execution, When the daily triage runs, Then every failure has a severity, a named owner and a target date by end of the triage And the burn-down is published to the sponsor the same day
  • error — Given a defect disputed as works-as-designed, When triage reviews it, Then the decision is recorded against the acceptance criterion the case tests And disputed items older than 3 business days escalate to the engagement manager
  • edge — Edge — repeat failure: Given a fix fails retest twice, When the second failure is logged, Then the defect escalates to review with the architect And the impact on the sign-off date is stated in the next status report
NFRs: Burn-down published daily; defect log links each entry to its test case and criterion
 3.3.3 UAT defect triage & retest

nfrs: Evidence (screenshot or export) attached to every executed case result
assumptions: D: client provides 4 trained testers for 2 weeks — if slipped: UAT extends day-for-day

stories.want: run a daily triage of failed cases with severities, owners and a published burn-down
stories.soThat: defects move to closure on a visible clock instead of piling up

ac.text: Given failed UAT cases from the day's execution, When the daily triage runs, Then every failure has a severity, a named owner and a target date by end of the triage And the burn-down is published to the sponsor the same day

Given a defect disputed as works-as-designed, When triage reviews it, Then the decision is recorded against the acceptance criterion the case tests And disputed items older than 3 business days escalate to the engagement manager

Edge — repeat failure: Given a fix fails retest twice, When the second failure is logged, Then the defect escalates to review with the architect And the impact on the sign-off date is stated in the next status report

nfrs: Burn-down published daily; defect log links each entry to its test case and criterion
assumptions: A: fixes are retested within 2 business days — impact if false: the UAT window extends and sign-off moves

stories.want: execute the cutover runbook and run a 2-week hypercare rota
stories.soThat: the first weeks of live operation have named cover and a visible issue burn-down

ac.text: Given UAT sign-off And an approved cutover runbook, When go-live executes, Then every runbook step completes with a timestamped owner And a go/no-go decision is recorded at the final gate And the hypercare rota is published before day 1
Given a cutover step fails its verification, When the failure is detected, Then the documented rollback for that step executes And the go/no-go gate is re-run before proceeding

Edge — issue surge: Given more than 10 issues open on any hypercare day, When the daily review runs, Then a severity triage is published by 9am the next business day And every S1 issue has a named owner within 2 working hours

nfrs: Hypercare issue log visible to the client sponsor; daily summary distributed by 9am
assumptions: A: hypercare is 2 weeks as priced — impact if false: an extension is a change order at the stated weekly rate

tasks.name: Kick-off & Discovery
tasks.description: Confirm scope, governance cadence, decision-makers and success measures with the client sponsor.
tasks.acceptance: Charter signed by the sponsor; minutes with owners and due dates distributed within 24 hours.

tasks.name: Stakeholder Interviews
tasks.description: Interview at least 8 stakeholders across sales, service and marketing on current workflows and pain points.
tasks.acceptance: Findings pack per function, pain points ranked by frequency, circulated within 2 business days of the last interview.

tasks.name: Requirements Workshop
tasks.description: Facilitated session converting interview findings into testable, MoSCoW-prioritized requirement statements.
tasks.acceptance: Requirements register signed by the client within 5 business days of the workshop.

tasks.name: Solution Design
tasks.description: Map every signed requirement to a configuration decision; flag anything needing custom build with effort and owner.
tasks.acceptance: Every Must-have requirement traces to a design section; client approves in writing within 5 business days of review.

tasks.name: Data Mapping
tasks.description: Field-level mapping from the legacy CRM: target, transform rule or explicit drop decision for every in-scope field; profiling on sampled rows.
tasks.acceptance: Client data steward approves the spec; fields failing validation in >2% of sampled rows carry a recorded cleanup decision.

tasks.name: Integration Testing
tasks.description: Execute the integration suite against the configured system; log, fix and retest defects before client testers enter.
tasks.acceptance: 100% of planned cases executed with recorded results; zero open S1/S2 defects at UAT entry.

tasks.name: Go-Live & Hypercare
tasks.description: Execute the cutover runbook with go/no-go gates, then run a 2-week hypercare rota with daily issue triage.
tasks.acceptance: Every runbook step completed with a timestamped owner; hypercare daily summary distributed by 9am.

tasks.name: Data migration build & dry run
tasks.description: Build extract-transform-load per the mapping spec; dry-run into UAT with per-object reconciliation and an exceptions file.
tasks.acceptance: Counts reconcile within 0.1% per object; exceptions quarantined with row, rule and suggested fix.

tasks.name: Core workflow configuration
tasks.description: Configure case categories, required fields, queue assignment rules and status flows per the approved design.
tasks.acceptance: A saved case auto-assigns to its mapped queue within 5 seconds; missing required fields reject the save inline.

tasks.name: Access model & queue setup
tasks.description: Configure role-based access: agents see their own queues, managers see all; access attempts outside role are logged.
tasks.acceptance: Own-queue visibility verified per role; out-of-queue access attempts recorded with user and timestamp.

tasks.name: Tester training session
tasks.description: Half-day guided session in the loaded UAT environment; each tester runs one case end-to-end; 10-question check.
tasks.acceptance: Attendance and check score recorded per tester; only testers scoring ≥7/10 execute UAT cases.

tasks.name: UAT defect triage & retest
tasks.description: Daily triage of failed cases: severity, owner, target date; retest after fix; burn-down published to the sponsor.
tasks.acceptance: Every failure has severity, named owner and target date by end of triage; disputed items escalate after 3 business days.

tasks.name: TC AC-6.1 — happy path: migrated counts reconcile to legacy within 0.1%
tasks.description:
1. Open the migration reconciliation report for the latest UAT run.
2. Compare per-object counts (accounts, contacts, cases) to the legacy extract totals in the mapping spec.
3. Open the 5 sampled cases listed in UAT workbook tab "Sample-6.1" and check owner, status and activity history.
tasks.acceptance: Counts within 0.1% per object; all 5 sampled cases show owner, status and full history.

tasks.name: TC AC-6.2 — error path: invalid legacy record quarantined with stated reason
tasks.description:
1. Load the exception seed file uat_bad_records.csv (2 rows: missing owner, malformed date) into the migration dry-run.
2. Run the dry-run migration.
3. Open the exceptions file from the run output.
tasks.acceptance: Both seeded records quarantined with source row, rule violated and suggested fix; the run completes without aborting.

tasks.name: TC AC-6.3 — edge: 24-month boundary records included, older excluded
tasks.description:
1. Locate the 3 boundary records dated exactly 24 months before cutover (workbook tab "Sample-6.3").
2. Run the extract build.
3. Check the reconciliation report totals for included vs excluded records.
tasks.acceptance: Boundary records included; older records excluded; both totals appear on the reconciliation report.

tasks.name: TC AC-6.4 — performance: p95 case page render ≤ 2 s at 50 concurrent users
tasks.description:
1. Start the 50-user load script (load_uat_50.jmx) against the UAT org.
2. During the 30-minute window, open the timed case page set every 5 minutes.
3. Export the p95 render timing from the run report.
tasks.acceptance: p95 case page render is 2 seconds or less across the full 30-minute window at 50 concurrent users.

tasks.name: TC AC-10.1 — happy path: saved case auto-assigns to mapped queue in 5 s
tasks.description:
1. Log in as tester uat_agent01.
2. Create a case with category "Billing dispute" and all required fields (data sheet "Case-A").
3. Save, then open the case history.
tasks.acceptance: Case lands in the Billing queue within 5 seconds; the history shows the assignment rule name.

tasks.name: TC AC-10.2 — error path: save without required field rejected inline
tasks.description:
1. Log in as uat_agent01.
2. Create a case leaving "Category" empty.
3. Attempt to save.
tasks.acceptance: Save is rejected with the missing field named inline; no partial case record is created.

tasks.name: TC AC-11.1 — happy path: agent sees own-queue cases only, totals match manager
tasks.description:
1. Log in as uat_agent02 (billing queue only).
2. Open the case list.
3. Compare the queue total to the manager view (uat_mgr01) for the billing queue.
tasks.acceptance: Only billing-queue cases are listed; the total matches the manager view for that queue.

tasks.name: TC AC-11.2 — error path: out-of-queue direct link blocked and logged
tasks.description:
1. As uat_agent02, paste the direct URL of case C-1042 (service queue).
2. Attempt to open it.
3. As uat_mgr01, open the access log.
tasks.acceptance: The case is not displayed; the access log records the attempt with user and timestamp.

tasks.name: TC AC-10.3 — edge: unmapped category routes to triage and is reported
tasks.description:
1. As uat_agent01, raise a case with category "Unmapped-Test" (no queue mapping).
2. Save the case and note the queue it lands in.
3. Open the next daily unmapped-category report.
tasks.acceptance: The case routes to the triage queue, and the daily report lists the unmapped category with the case reference.

tasks.name: TC AC-11.3 — edge: role change mid-shift swaps the visible queue within 15 min
tasks.description:
1. As uat_mgr01, move uat_agent02 from the billing queue to the service queue.
2. As uat_agent02, refresh the case list and start a 15-minute timer.
3. Compare the visible cases before and after the refresh.
tasks.acceptance: Service-queue cases appear and billing-queue cases disappear within 15 minutes, with no re-login required.
